# PrintxPDF

> Free browser-based tools for printing web pages without ads and for working with PDF files. Every tool runs client-side in the visitor's browser using pdf-lib, pdf.js and Tesseract.js — files are never uploaded to a server.

PrintxPDF has two halves: a web-page cleaner that extracts an article with Mozilla Readability and lets you delete anything left before printing or saving as PDF, and 29 PDF tools covering merge, split, organise, compress, OCR, sign, watermark, convert and QR generation. Tools that genuinely require a server (PowerPoint, EPUB and MOBI conversion) are labelled as demo interfaces rather than pretending to work.

## Tools
- [Merge PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/merge-pdf): Combine files into one. Combine multiple PDF files into one organized document, in the order you choose.
- [Split PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/split-pdf): Break into ranges or pages. Break a PDF into page ranges, single pages, or every N pages. Get a ZIP-free set of downloads.
- [Organize Pages](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/organize-pdf): Reorder, rotate, delete. See every page as a thumbnail. Drag to reorder, rotate any page, delete what you don't need.
- [Rotate PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/rotate-pdf): Turn all pages. Rotate every page in a PDF by 90, 180 or 270 degrees.
- [Delete Pages](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/delete-pages): Remove pages by number. Remove specific pages or ranges from a PDF.
- [Extract Pages](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/extract-pages): Keep only what you need. Pull out specific pages into a new PDF.
- [Compress PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/compress-pdf): Shrink file size. Reduce the size of your PDF by rewriting it with compressed object streams, dropping metadata and, optionally, downsampling images.
- [OCR PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/ocr-pdf): Make scans searchable. Turn scanned PDFs and images into searchable, selectable text with on-device optical character recognition.
- [PDF Reader](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/pdf-reader): Open & read online. Open and read PDFs with smooth navigation, zoom and page thumbnails. No install needed.
- [PDF to JPG](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/pdf-to-jpg): Pages → images. Export PDF pages as high-quality JPG or PNG images for email, slides and the web.
- [JPG to PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/jpg-to-pdf): Images → one PDF. Combine JPG, PNG and WebP images into a single clean PDF. Ideal for scans, receipts and photo sets.
- [Word to PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/word-to-pdf): DOCX → PDF. Convert Word documents to PDFs that look the same everywhere. Links, images and styles intact.
- [Excel to PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/excel-to-pdf): XLSX → PDF. Convert Excel spreadsheets to polished PDFs for sharing, printing and archiving.
- [HTML to PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/html-to-pdf): Web files → PDF. Turn an HTML file or pasted markup into a clean PDF using the same engine as our web-page printer.
- [PDF to Text](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/pdf-to-text): Extract all text. Pull every line of text out of a PDF into a plain .txt file you can search and reuse.
- [Sign PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/sign-pdf): Draw or type a signature. Add typed or drawn signatures, names and dates. Download a professional file ready to share.
- [Add Watermark](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/add-watermark): Stamp text on pages. Stamp PDFs with text. Adjust size, opacity, rotation and color to mark drafts, copies and confidential pages.
- [Page Numbers](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/page-numbers): Add numbering. Stamp page numbers on every page, in the position and format you choose.
- [Edit Metadata](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/edit-metadata): Title, author, keywords. Set the title, author, subject and keywords stored inside a PDF.
- [Flatten PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/flatten-pdf): Bake forms & annotations. Flatten form fields so they can no longer be edited, and fix a PDF for archiving.
- [Remove Metadata](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/remove-metadata): Scrub personal info. Strip author, creator, keywords and timestamps from a PDF before you share it.
- [QR Code Generator](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/tools/qr-code): Print-ready QR codes. Create print-ready QR codes for links, WiFi, contact cards, email and SMS. Free, right in your browser.

## Guides
### Printing web pages
To print a web page without ads, open it in a printer-friendly tool or your browser Reader mode first, then print. This removes navigation, ads and sidebars and typically cuts a nine-page printout to two or three pages while keeping the article text and images intact.
- [How to print a web page without ads](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/print-web-pages/print-web-page-without-ads): Paste the page URL into a printer-friendly tool, or turn on your browser Reader mode, then press Ctrl+P. Both strip ads, menus and sidebars before the page reaches your printer, usually reducing a long article from eight or nine sheets to two or three.
- [How to print only the part of a page you selected](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/print-web-pages/print-selected-text-only): Highlight the text you want, press Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on Mac), and choose "Selection only" under the pages option in the print dialog. Chrome, Firefox and Edge all support this. Safari uses "Print Selected Text" from the File menu after you select.
- [Web page printing problems and how to fix them](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/print-web-pages/fix-web-page-printing-problems): Most web page printing problems come from three causes: the page is wider than the paper, background graphics are disabled, or the site has no print stylesheet. Fix them by switching to landscape, lowering the scale to 80 percent, enabling background graphics, or printing through a printer-friendly view.
- [Print to paper or save as PDF? How to decide](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/print-web-pages/print-web-page-to-pdf-vs-printer): Save as PDF when you need to search, share, archive or keep a dated record. Print on paper when you need to annotate by hand, read away from a screen, or produce something for a physical file. A PDF costs nothing, is searchable, and can always be printed later.

### Saving web pages as PDF
Press Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on Mac), change the destination to "Save as PDF" and click Save. On iPhone, use the Share sheet, tap Options and choose PDF. Both keep the text selectable and the links clickable, unlike a screenshot, which stores pixels only.
- [How to save a web page as a PDF in any browser](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/save-webpage-as-pdf/save-webpage-as-pdf-chrome): Press Ctrl+P on Windows or Cmd+P on a Mac, open the Destination list and choose Save as PDF, then click Save. Every desktop browser supports this. The resulting file keeps selectable text and clickable links, and you can limit it to a page range before saving.
- [How to save a web page as a PDF on iPhone and iPad](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/save-webpage-as-pdf/save-webpage-as-pdf-iphone): On iPhone and iPad, open the page in Safari, tap the Share button, tap Options under the page title, choose PDF, then tap Save to Files. For a picture-perfect copy instead, take a screenshot, tap the thumbnail, switch to Full Page and save the PDF.
- [How to take a full-page screenshot of a website](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/save-webpage-as-pdf/full-page-screenshot): In Chrome, open DevTools with F12, press Ctrl+Shift+P, type screenshot and choose Capture full size screenshot. Firefox and Edge have it built in: right-click the page and pick Take Screenshot, then Save full page. The result is one tall PNG of the entire scrolling page.
- [How to archive a web page so it still exists later](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/save-webpage-as-pdf/archive-web-pages): Archive a web page three ways at once: submit it to the Wayback Machine for a public, third-party-dated copy; save your own PDF for a readable offline record; and keep a full-page screenshot as visual proof. Public archives fail on paywalled or logged-in pages, so the local copy matters.

### Merging PDF files
Add every PDF to a merge tool, drag the files into the order you want, then merge and download one combined file. Pages keep their internal order within each file, so the file list decides everything. A browser-based merge runs locally, so nothing is uploaded to a server.
- [How to merge PDF files for free](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/merge-pdf/how-to-merge-pdf-files): Open a browser merge tool, add every PDF you want to combine, drag the files into the order you need, then click Merge and download the single output file. Order is decided by the file list, top to bottom, and pages inside each file keep their own order.
- [How to combine PDFs without Adobe Acrobat](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/merge-pdf/merge-pdf-without-acrobat): macOS can merge PDFs for free in Preview: open one file, show Thumbnails, drag the second PDF into the sidebar, then use File, Export as PDF. Windows 11 has no built-in merge and Google Drive cannot combine files either, so on those platforms use a free browser-based merge tool.
- [How to combine images and PDFs into one document](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/merge-pdf/combine-images-and-pdfs): Convert the images to PDF pages first, then merge them with your existing PDFs. A JPG, PNG or HEIC becomes a one-page PDF sized to the image, and once every input is a PDF you can drag all of them into a single ordered document and download one file.
- [How to reorder, rotate and delete PDF pages](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/merge-pdf/reorder-pdf-pages): Open the PDF in a page organiser, drag the page thumbnails into the order you want, use the rotate buttons for any sideways page, select unwanted pages and delete them, then download. Rotation is stored as a page property, so a rotated page stays rotated in every viewer and on paper.

### Splitting and extracting PDF pages
Open the PDF in a split tool and choose a mode: single pages, custom ranges such as 1-3,5,8-, or every N pages. Extracting keeps the chosen pages in one new file; splitting produces several files. The original on your disk is never modified by any of them.
- [How to split a PDF into separate pages or ranges](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/split-pdf/split-pdf-into-pages): Open the PDF in a split tool, choose a mode, and download the results. Three modes cover almost everything: split into single pages, split by custom ranges such as 1-3,5,8-, or split every N pages into equal chunks. Output arrives as separate PDFs or one ZIP archive.
- [How to extract specific pages from a PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/split-pdf/extract-pages-from-pdf): Open the PDF in an extract tool, tick the pages you want or type a range like 4-9, then download a new PDF containing only those pages. The original is untouched. Extracting differs from splitting: you keep one file with a chosen subset instead of many files.
- [How to delete pages from a PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/split-pdf/delete-pages-from-pdf): Open the PDF in a page editor, select the thumbnails of the pages you want gone or type a range such as 2,5,11-13, then delete and download. Deleting pages from a copy is safe: the original file on your disk is unchanged until you replace it yourself.
- [How to split a large PDF to get under an email size limit](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/split-pdf/split-large-pdf-for-email): Gmail allows 25 MB per message and Outlook.com allows 20 MB, but Base64 encoding inflates attachments by about a third, so aim for 18 MB or less. Compress the PDF first; if it is still too big, split it into numbered parts that each land under that ceiling.

### Compressing PDF files
Compress a PDF by choosing between two methods. Lossless structural compression subsets fonts and removes unused objects, typically saving 10-30 percent with zero visible change. Image downsampling re-encodes embedded photos at a lower DPI, which can cut a scanned document by 80-95 percent but is not reversible.
- [How to compress a PDF file for free](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/compress-pdf/how-to-compress-a-pdf): To compress a PDF for free, open it in a browser-based compressor and pick one of two methods. Lossless structural compression subsets fonts and strips unused objects without touching a pixel. Image downsampling re-encodes photos at a lower DPI. Text documents shrink 10-30 percent; scans can drop by 90.
- [How to reduce a PDF file size for email](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/compress-pdf/reduce-pdf-file-size-for-email): Compress the PDF to a 150 DPI target first, which is enough for on-screen reading and usually gets a scan under 5 MB. Gmail and Yahoo cap attachments at 25 MB, Outlook.com and iCloud Mail at 20 MB, and MIME encoding adds about 33 percent, so aim below 18 MB.
- [How to compress a PDF without losing quality](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/compress-pdf/compress-pdf-without-losing-quality): Truly lossless PDF compression means font subsetting, object streams and removing unused objects — it changes nothing visible and saves 10-30 percent. Anything beyond that downsamples images. For documents you will only read on screen, 150 DPI is visually indistinguishable from 300 and saves about 75 percent.
- [Why is my PDF file so large? 8 reasons](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/compress-pdf/why-is-my-pdf-so-large): A PDF is usually large for one of eight reasons: it is a scan stored as images, images are embedded at full resolution, fonts are embedded whole instead of subset, resources are duplicated per page, saves were incremental, images are cropped only visually, forms and attachments are attached, or colour profiles and transparency are heavy.

### Converting PDF to other formats
Converting out of PDF works best when the file has a real text layer and a simple layout. Word and Google Docs both open PDFs directly and rebuild the text well. Tables need column detection or Power Query. Scanned PDFs must be OCR-ed first, and slide conversion needs Acrobat or a desktop app.
- [How to convert a PDF to Word and keep the formatting](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/convert-from-pdf/pdf-to-word): Microsoft Word converts PDFs itself: File → Open, choose the PDF, and accept the prompt. Google Docs does the same through Drive. Both rebuild single-column text well and struggle with multi-column layouts, text boxes and tables. If nothing is editable afterwards, the PDF is a scan and needs OCR first.
- [How to convert a PDF table into Excel](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/convert-from-pdf/pdf-to-excel): On Windows with Microsoft 365, use Data → Get Data → From File → From PDF, which reads tables natively. Otherwise copy the table, paste into Excel, and split it with Data → Text to Columns. Both need a real text layer — scanned tables must be OCR-ed first, and messy tables are often faster to retype.
- [How to extract all the text from a PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/convert-from-pdf/pdf-to-text): First test whether the PDF has a text layer: try to select a sentence. If text highlights, drop the file into a text extractor and export a .txt — you get every page at once with the reading order preserved. If nothing highlights, the pages are images and you must run OCR before any extraction will work.
- [How to turn a PDF into PowerPoint slides](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/convert-from-pdf/pdf-to-powerpoint): There is no free, reliable way to turn a PDF into slides with editable text boxes — that requires Adobe Acrobat Pro or a server-side converter. The method that always works is to export each PDF page as an image at 150-200 DPI and place one image per slide, which PowerPoint automates with Insert → Photo Album.

### Converting files to PDF
Every major application exports PDF directly: Word uses File → Save As → PDF, Excel uses Export → Create PDF/XPS after setting a print area, browsers use Ctrl+P with "Save as PDF" as the destination, and images can be combined into a single PDF. The settings that matter are font embedding, scale-to-fit and DPI.
- [How to convert Word to PDF and keep the fonts](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/convert-to-pdf/word-to-pdf): In Word, use File → Save As and pick PDF, or File → Export → Create PDF/XPS. Word embeds every font it can automatically. On macOS choose "Best for electronic distribution and accessibility" rather than printing to PDF, because the print route drops hyperlinks and accessibility tags.
- [How to convert an Excel spreadsheet to PDF that actually fits](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/convert-to-pdf/excel-to-pdf): Set a print area, then use Page Layout → Scale to Fit with Width set to 1 page and Height left on Automatic. Add repeating header rows through Print Titles, switch to landscape for wide tables, and export with File → Export → Create PDF/XPS. Never set both Width and Height to 1 page.
- [How to convert HTML to PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/convert-to-pdf/html-to-pdf): For a one-off, press Ctrl+P and set the destination to "Save as PDF" — the browser renders real text and clickable links. For repeatable output, control pagination with @page and break-inside CSS, and drive headless Chrome or Puppeteer so every run produces an identical file.
- [How to combine photos and scans into one PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/convert-to-pdf/images-to-pdf): Drop your JPG or PNG files into an image-to-PDF tool, put them in the right order, and pick a page size. Choose A4 or Letter with each image fitted to the page for documents, and 300 DPI if the result will be printed. HEIC files from an iPhone must be converted to JPEG first in most browsers.

### PDFs and images
To turn a PDF page into an image, render it at a chosen resolution: 144 DPI for screens, 300 DPI for printing. To recover a photo that was placed in the PDF, extract the embedded image instead, which returns the original pixels without re-rendering or quality loss.
- [How to convert PDF pages to JPG or PNG images](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/pdf-images/pdf-to-jpg): Open the PDF in a converter, choose a resolution, and export. Use 144 DPI for screens and email, 300 DPI for printing. Choose PNG for pages that are mostly text, tables or diagrams, and JPG for pages dominated by photographs, where it is roughly three times smaller.
- [How to extract the original images from a PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/pdf-images/extract-images-from-pdf): Extraction pulls the embedded image object out of the PDF byte for byte, so a photo saved as a JPEG inside the file comes back as the same JPEG at its original pixel size. Rendering instead repaints the whole page at a resolution you choose, which resamples the photo and adds the surrounding text and margins.
- [PNG vs JPG for PDF pages: which should you pick?](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/pdf-images/pdf-to-png-transparent): Choose PNG when the page contains text, tables, line art or screenshots, or when you need a transparent background: it is lossless and keeps letter edges perfectly sharp. Choose JPG when the page is dominated by photographs, where it produces a file roughly three times smaller with no visible difference.
- [What resolution and format do you need for printing?](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/pdf-images/best-image-format-for-print): For anything held in the hand, supply 300 pixels per inch of final print size: 2480 × 3508 px for A4, 2550 × 3300 px for US Letter, 1200 × 1800 px for a 4 × 6 photo. Posters viewed from a metre away are fine at 150 DPI. Upscaling invents pixels and does not add real detail.

### Signing PDFs
To sign a PDF without printing it, open the file in a signing tool, create a signature by drawing, typing or uploading a transparent PNG, drag it onto the signature line, add the date, then flatten and download. In most countries this carries the same legal weight as ink on paper.
- [How to sign a PDF without printing it](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/sign-pdf/how-to-sign-a-pdf): Open the PDF in a signing tool, create your signature by drawing it with a mouse or finger, typing it in a handwriting font, or uploading a transparent PNG. Drag it onto the signature line, resize it to about the height of the surrounding text, add the date, then flatten and download.
- [Are electronic signatures legally binding?](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/sign-pdf/electronic-signature-legally-binding): Yes, in most cases. In the US the ESIGN Act and state UETA adoptions give electronic signatures the same legal effect as ink for most agreements. In the EU, eIDAS says a signature cannot be denied validity merely for being electronic. Wills, certain property and family-law documents remain excluded.
- [How to create a clean signature image with a transparent background](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/sign-pdf/create-a-signature-image): Sign a sheet of unlined white paper with a black pen, photograph it in flat daylight, crop tight, raise the contrast until the paper is pure white, then delete the white to alpha and export as PNG-24. Aim for around 1000 px wide so it stays sharp when printed.
- [How to fill in and sign a PDF form](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/sign-pdf/fill-and-sign-a-form): First find out which kind of form you have. If clicking a blank produces a text cursor, it is an interactive AcroForm: type into the fields and tab between them. If nothing happens, it is a flat scan, so add free text boxes on top instead. Flatten the file afterwards either way.

### OCR and scanned documents
OCR converts the pixels of a scanned page into machine-readable characters and stores them as an invisible text layer aligned with the image. The page still looks identical, but it becomes searchable, selectable and copyable. Accuracy runs above 98 percent on clean 300 DPI print and far lower on handwriting.
- [How to OCR a scanned PDF so you can search it](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/ocr-scanned-documents/how-to-ocr-a-scanned-pdf): Run the PDF through an OCR tool, choose the language of the document, and export. The tool reads each page image, recognises the characters, and writes them back as an invisible text layer positioned over the picture. The page looks unchanged but becomes searchable, selectable and copyable.
- [How to extract text from an image or photo](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/ocr-scanned-documents/extract-text-from-image): On a Mac or iPhone, select the text directly in the image using Live Text. On Windows 11, open the screenshot in Snipping Tool and use Text actions. Anywhere else, right-click the image in Chrome and choose Search with Google Lens, then copy the text it detects.
- [How to tell if a PDF is searchable, and make it so](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/ocr-scanned-documents/make-pdf-searchable): Press Ctrl+F and search for a word you can see on the page. If it is not found, try to select the text with your mouse. If the cursor only draws a rectangle instead of highlighting words, the PDF is image-only and needs OCR to become searchable.
- [How to get better OCR results from bad scans](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/ocr-scanned-documents/improve-ocr-accuracy): Scan at 300 DPI, straighten the page to within half a degree, raise the contrast until the paper is white and the ink black, process one column at a time, and select only the language actually present. Input quality dominates every engine setting you can change afterwards.

### Watermarks, page numbers and stamps
To mark a PDF, add a watermark for a visual warning, page numbers for navigation, and a header or footer for identifying details such as a company name or file reference. All three are drawn onto the existing pages, so they change how the file looks without changing the underlying text.
- [How to add a watermark to a PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/watermark-page-numbers/add-watermark-to-pdf): To add a watermark to a PDF, open the file in a watermark tool, type the text you want such as DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL, set opacity to around 15 percent and rotation to 45 degrees, choose centred or tiled placement, then apply it to every page and save the result.
- [How to add page numbers to a PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/watermark-page-numbers/add-page-numbers-to-pdf): To add page numbers to a PDF, open it in a page numbering tool, pick a position such as bottom centre, choose a format such as "1 of 12", set the starting number and the first page to number, then apply. The numbers are drawn onto each page and cannot shift later.
- [How to add a header or footer to a PDF](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/watermark-page-numbers/add-header-footer-pdf): To add a header or footer to a PDF, open it in a header and footer tool, type the text for the left, centre and right positions, set a margin of about 36 points from the paper edge, then apply it to the pages you want. Headers and footers are drawn onto each page as real text.
- [Watermark, stamp, or redaction? Choosing the right mark](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/watermark-page-numbers/watermark-vs-stamp): A watermark warns every reader about the whole document. A stamp records a specific action on a specific page, such as approved or received. Redaction removes content from the file permanently. Only redaction changes what the file contains; the other two only change how it looks.

### PDF privacy and security
Before sharing a PDF, strip the document metadata, redact any sensitive content properly by removing it rather than covering it, and use encryption only when you genuinely need to control who can open the file. Always verify redaction by trying to select and copy the text afterwards.
- [How to remove hidden metadata from a PDF before sharing](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/pdf-privacy/remove-metadata-from-pdf): To remove metadata from a PDF, open it in a metadata tool and clear the Title, Author, Subject, Keywords, Creator and Producer fields along with the XMP block, then save. Embedded image EXIF and GPS data survive that step, so rasterise or re-encode the images if photos are involved.
- [How to password protect a PDF, and what it actually protects](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/pdf-privacy/password-protect-pdf): A PDF supports two passwords: a user password that is required to open the file and genuinely encrypts it, and an owner password that only sets permissions such as printing. Only the user password protects the content. Permissions are advisory and any determined tool can ignore them.
- [How to redact a PDF so the text is really gone](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/pdf-privacy/redact-pdf-properly): To redact a PDF, the sensitive content must be deleted from the file, not covered. Cover the areas with solid black, then rasterise every page to an image and rebuild the PDF, which destroys the text layer. Verify by selecting all text and pasting it into a text editor.
- [Are online PDF tools safe? What happens to your file](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/pdf-privacy/are-online-pdf-tools-safe): It depends entirely on whether the tool uploads your file or processes it in your browser. Upload-based sites send the document to a server that could store or read it. Browser-based tools never transmit the file at all. You can tell which is which in thirty seconds using the network tab.

### Printing recipes
To print a recipe cleanly, use the site's own Print Recipe button if the recipe sits in a recipe card, since it opens a stripped-down version. If there is no button, paste the page address into a printer-friendly tool, delete the story and the photos, and print the result as one page.
- [How to print a recipe without the life story and ads](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/print-recipes/print-recipe-without-ads): Look for a Print Recipe button on the recipe card first, because it opens a stripped-down version with just the ingredients and method. If the site has no button, paste the page address into a printer-friendly tool, delete the story and photos, and print. Either way you get one page instead of eight.
- [How to print a recipe without the pictures](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/print-recipes/print-recipe-without-pictures): To print a recipe without pictures, use a printer-friendly tool and set images to none, or open the site's own print view and untick "include images". Browsers have no images-off switch of their own, so turning off background graphics only removes decorative images, not the recipe photos.
- [How to build a printed recipe binder that survives a kitchen](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/print-recipes/make-a-recipe-binder): Build a recipe binder by printing every recipe to one consistent format on one side of a sheet, filing them in top-loading sheet protectors inside a two-inch D-ring binder, dividing by category, and keeping a printed index at the front that you update when you add a recipe.
- [How to make a weekly meal plan and shopping list you can print](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/print-recipes/meal-plan-printables): Build a one-page plan with seven day columns and rows for the meals you actually plan, put an aisle-grouped shopping list on the reverse, and merge the week's recipes into a single PDF behind it. Print one copy for the fridge and one for the shop.

### Students and research
Students save the most paper by printing academic PDFs two pages per sheet and double-sided, which turns a 24-page paper into six sheets. Annotate the PDF rather than the paper copy so highlights stay searchable, and record the author, title, date, URL and access date for every web source you cite.
- [How to print journal articles and papers properly](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/students-research/print-journal-articles): Open the PDF in a real reader rather than the journal website, then print two pages per sheet, double-sided, in greyscale. That turns a 24-page paper into six sheets. Add a binding margin if you will punch or staple it, and test on the first four pages before running the rest.
- [How to annotate PDFs for studying](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/students-research/annotate-pdf-for-study): Read once without marking anything, then highlight on a second pass using a fixed colour code and write a margin note in your own words beside every highlight. Use Zotero or Adobe Acrobat Reader on a laptop, GoodNotes or Notability on an iPad, and export the highlights into your notes before revision starts.
- [How to cite a web page in APA, MLA and Chicago](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/students-research/cite-a-web-page): Every web page citation needs five things: author, date of publication, page title, site name and URL. APA 7th puts the date in brackets after the author, MLA 9th puts the site name in italics and drops the https prefix, and Chicago 17th offers both a footnote and a bibliography form. Add an access date only when there is no publication date.
- [How to print lecture slides without wasting 60 pages](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/students-research/print-lecture-slides): Use handout mode rather than full-page slides: three per sheet if you want ruled note lines, six per sheet for revision. Delete the duplicate pages that animation build steps create in a PDF export, and print in greyscale so dark slide backgrounds do not drain a cartridge. Sixty slides then fit on five duplexed sheets.

### For publishers and developers
Give readers a print button and a print stylesheet. The button is a plain HTML anchor or a button calling window.print(), placed near the article title. The stylesheet hides navigation, resets the layout to a single column, sets @page margins, controls page breaks and prints link URLs so the paper copy stands on its own.
- [How to add a print button to WordPress](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/publishers-wordpress/add-print-button-to-wordpress): The quickest route is a Custom HTML block containing a single anchor tag, which works on any theme with no plugin. For a button on every post, register a shortcode in a child theme or site-specific plugin and append it with the_content filter. WooCommerce order pages need window.print() instead, because they are login-gated.
- [How to write a print stylesheet that actually works](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/publishers-wordpress/print-stylesheet-css): Wrap print rules in @media print, hide navigation and widgets, reset the article container to a single block-level column, set margins with @page, and control pagination with break-inside: avoid on figures and break-after: avoid on headings. Ship the legacy page-break-* aliases alongside the modern properties, because engines still disagree.
- [How to make your website printer-friendly](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/publishers-wordpress/printer-friendly-website-design): Open your own pages in print preview and fix what you see: hide navigation and widgets, override dark-mode colours, expand link URLs, keep tables and figures whole, load lazy images, and print the page title, URL and date. Most sites fail because nobody has ever looked at the preview.
- [How to add a print or PDF button to any website](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/publishers-wordpress/print-button-any-website): Paste a single anchor tag that opens the current URL in a printer-friendly view, or a button element calling window.print(). Both are a few lines of plain HTML and work in any CMS or static site. Hide the button in @media print, and use the anchor form inside Wix, where embeds are iframes.

### Saving paper and ink
The four settings that matter most are duplex, greyscale, draft quality and pages per sheet. Applied together they typically cut the cost of a document by 70 to 90 percent. Set them as your printer defaults rather than per job, and use print preview and page ranges to avoid printing pages nobody reads.
- [How to save ink when printing](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/save-paper-ink/save-ink-when-printing): Set draft quality and black ink only as your printer defaults, turn off background graphics, remove decorative images, and use a narrow serif font like Garamond at 11pt. Together these typically cut ink use by half or more on ordinary documents, without changing anything about how readable the page is.
- [How to print double-sided, including without a duplex printer](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/save-paper-ink/print-double-sided): If your printer has a duplex unit, tick "Print on both sides" and choose Flip on long edge for portrait documents. Without one, print the odd pages, put the stack back in the tray, then print the even pages in reverse order. Test on four pages before committing to a long document.
- [How to fit more on a printed page without making it unreadable](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/save-paper-ink/fit-more-on-a-page): Cut the margins first, since it is free: moving from one inch to half an inch adds about 28 percent more text area on A4. Then drop the scale to 90 or 80 percent, and only then consider two pages per sheet. Keep body text at 9pt or larger for anything you will read continuously.
- [How to print less and waste less](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/save-paper-ink/eco-friendly-printing): The largest single win is changing your printer defaults to duplex and greyscale, because it applies to every job without anyone remembering. After that, look at print preview before every job, print page ranges rather than whole documents, and give yourself a PDF-first folder that you print from only after 24 hours.

### QR codes for print
A printed QR code scans reliably when it is exported as vector, printed at least 2 cm wide, surrounded by a four-module quiet zone, and set in dark ink on a light background. Use the 10:1 rule: the code must be at least one tenth of the scanning distance.
- [How to make a QR code that actually scans off paper](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/qr-codes/qr-code-for-print): Export the QR code as vector SVG, print it at least 2 cm (0.8 in) wide, keep a quiet zone of four blank modules on every side, and use dark ink on a light background. Choose error correction level M for most jobs, then scan a real test print before running the full batch.
- [How to make a WiFi QR code guests can scan](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/qr-codes/wifi-qr-code): A WiFi QR code encodes the plain text WIFI:T:WPA;S:NetworkName;P:Password;; and phones turn it into a one-tap join prompt. iPhones running iOS 11 or later and Android 10 or later read it with the built-in camera, so no app is needed on either side.
- [What size should a QR code be? The distance rule](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/qr-codes/qr-code-size-for-print): Use the 10:1 rule: a QR code must be at least one tenth as wide as the distance it is scanned from. A code read at 30 cm needs to be 3 cm wide; one read from 3 metres needs 30 cm. The absolute floor for any printed code is 2 cm.
- [How to put a QR code on a business card or flyer](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/qr-codes/qr-code-on-business-card): Encode a vCard for contact details or a short URL for a landing page, size the code at 20 to 25 mm, keep 5 mm of clear space around it and away from the trim edge, and supply vector artwork at 300 DPI with the modules in 100% black. Proof one card before ordering.

### Browser extensions and shortcuts
Firefox and Safari have built-in reader modes that produce clean printouts: press F9 in Firefox or Control-Command-R in Safari, then print. Chrome has no print-ready reader mode, so use a bookmarklet, an extension or a web-based cleaner. Bookmarklets need no permissions and work in every browser.
- [Print-friendly options for Google Chrome](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/browser-extensions/print-friendly-extension-chrome): Chrome has no print-ready reader mode, so the clean options are a bookmarklet, a Chrome Web Store extension, DevTools, or a web-based cleaner. A bookmarklet is the safest: it is one line of JavaScript in a bookmark, needs no permissions and cannot read pages you do not click it on.
- [Printing better from Firefox](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/browser-extensions/firefox-print-addon): Press F9 to switch Firefox into Reader View, which strips ads, menus and sidebars, then press Ctrl+P to print the clean layout. Firefox also exposes scale, margins, headers and footers and selection printing in its print modal, so most jobs need no add-on at all.
- [Printing better from Safari on Mac and iPhone](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/browser-extensions/safari-print-extension): On a Mac, press Control-Command-R for Safari Reader then Command-P to print the clean layout, or use File then Print Selected Text for one passage. On iPhone, tap Share, then Options at the top of the sheet, and choose Reader PDF to save the article without ads.
- [Bookmarklet vs browser extension: which should you use?](https://printxpdf.vercel.app/blog/browser-extensions/bookmarklet-vs-extension): Use a bookmarklet unless you need something an extension can only do. A bookmarklet is one line of JavaScript stored in a bookmark: it needs no permissions, runs only when you click it, works in every browser, and cannot be sold or updated behind your back. Extensions buy convenience with access.
